unit.why: A single anecdote: R. Nahman passes through a town with merchandise and leads prayers in the beit midrash without permission, which sparks a confrontation with the congregation.
unit.boundary_note: text is garbled near the end (the passage about the old rabbi, the Toldot author and R. Zalman); the story seems to end abruptly with R. Alexander's defence

stories.start_quote: שמעתי פ״א הלך ר׳ נחמן ז"ל
stories.end_quote: הניחו את האיש שהוא תמיד עם השם
stories.summary_en: R. Nahman, travelling with merchandise, enters a beit midrash during the morning service and leads the prayer in a new nusach without permission. His sweet words keep the angry congregation from removing him. Afterwards they rebuke him, and he answers sharply that no one can say their forefathers are in Paradise. R. Alexander, a disciple of R. Zalman, then defends him as a man who is always with God.
